events.title: The First Fleet sails for Australia
events.description: Captain Arthur Phillip led eleven ships out of Portsmouth, England, carrying convicts, marines and supplies. Their mission was to found a penal colony in New South Wales.
events.significance: The voyage led to the British settlement of Sydney in 1788. It began a colonial era that transformed Australia and profoundly affected its Indigenous peoples.

events.title: Ecuador declares independence
events.description: Ecuador separated from Gran Colombia and began life as a sovereign republic.
events.significance: The split ended the union of Colombia, Venezuela and Ecuador. It set Ecuador on its path as an independent nation.

events.title: First reported apparition at Fátima
events.description: Three shepherd children in Fátima, Portugal, said they saw a vision of the Virgin Mary. They reported further visions over the following months.
events.significance: Fátima became one of the world's major Catholic pilgrimage sites. The reported apparitions shaped 20th-century Catholic devotion.

events.title: The first Formula One World Championship race
events.description: The inaugural season of the Formula One World Championship began at Silverstone in Britain. Giuseppe Farina won the first drivers' title for Alfa Romeo.
events.significance: It launched what became the pinnacle of international motorsport. The championship has run every year since.

events.title: Pope John Paul II survives an assassination attempt
events.description: Mehmet Ali Ağca shot and seriously wounded the Pope in St. Peter's Square in Rome. The Pope survived after a five-hour operation. He later visited his attacker in prison.
events.significance: The shooting shocked the world and became one of the most dramatic moments of the Cold War era. The Pope's public forgiveness of his attacker became a lasting symbol of mercy.
